messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> page fired: PD-INC-9801 - 'queue_depth > 10k for service:request-dispatcher' - severity: P1 - routes: eng-oncall, eng-sre

pagerduty: Incident created: PD-INC-9801 (unacknowledged) - paging Zoe (primary)

Zoe: acked. I'm on it. seeing a spike in dispatcher queue depth in grafana (queue-length > 12k) and token generation latency rising.

Mike: hitting this now too, thanks. service pods are busy, CPU ~95% on dispatcher replicas. autoscaler not adding pods. HPA shows desired=50, current=20, "failed to scale" events in k8s.

Alex: any obvious kube events? `kubectl describe hpa dispatch` + `kubectl get events --namespace inference | tail -n 50`?

Zoe: runnning quick checks, pasting output:```hpa.dispatch/status: currentReplicas: 20 desiredReplicas: 50 lastScaleTime: 2026-03-15T10:18:12Z events: Warning ScalingFailed HorizontalPodAutoscaler failed to get CPU utilization: metrics API unavailable```

Sara: metrics API errors. we just pushed a cluster metrics-server bump last night in prod-2 region, maybe rollout partial. Could be metrics adapter flapping.

Mike: also seeing pending pods stuck in Pending with reason: Insufficient memory. Node autoscaler logs show node pool quota exhausted (cloud: GCP) - we've hit our regional quota for n1-highmem.

Zoe: so two failure modes: metrics API preventing HPA from reading CPU, and node quota preventing nodepool scale. Ok. Prioritize customer impact and live mitigation.

Alex: quick mitigation options: 1) manually scale dispatcher StatefulSet/Deployment to desiredReplicas temporarily 2) request emergency quota bump from cloud console (may take 10-30m) 3) failover traffic to dedicated region/backup endpoint 4) enable burst-capacity cluster (we have reserved burst capacity but it's gated).

Zoe: I'm going to roll manual scale now to relieve queue. `kubectl scale deploy/dispatcher --replicas=50 -n inference`

ops-bot: Executing: `kubectl scale deploy/dispatcher --replicas=50 -n inference`

Zoe: scaled to 50, pods are creating. Some pods pending due to scheduling: "0/40 nodes are available: Insufficient memory."

Mike: still blocked by node pool. New pods in Pending with `FailedScheduling`. Node autoscaler log shows: "node quota exceeded for project, cannot create nodes". Requesting quota bump in cloud console now and opening support ticket.

Sara: while quota comes through, we can try small-step degradation: reduce per-pod memory requests for dispatcher to fit more pods on existing nodes, or enable pod eviction strategy to prioritize lower-importance jobs. That requires a quick deploy + restart. Risky but might buy us 5k queue reduction.

Alex: I can patch a temporary resource-override. Suggest `kubectl set resources deploy/dispatcher -c dispatcher --limits=memory=6Gi --requests=memory=4Gi -n inference` then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/dispatcher`. Do a canary with one replica first.

Zoe: do it. I'll monitor queue and user-impact dashboards.

Alex: patch applied to the canary replica. Rolling out.

Mike: meanwhile, PD note: affected customers: high-volume inference jobs in prod-2; some 503s reported from app-proxy. Putting notice in #general to ask SREs to pause non-critical batch jobs.

Zoe: contacting on-call support in sales/customer-success: @sre-support please hold non-essential jobs and inform customers if needed.

Mike: ops ticket opened for quota: TKT-3421, submitted with priority 'severe', referencing PD-INC-9801. Cloud support said likely 15-25 minutes.

Sara: can we enable the reserved burst capacity? There's a toggle in console but requires an owner (enterprise). Who can flip it?

Zoe: I can request the toggle but it needs org-owner approval. Pinged org-owner in DM, no response yet.

Alex: can we throttle ingress instead? Add a temporary rate limit via api-gateway for non-critical routes to throttle new requests and let queued ones drain.

Zoe: doing that now: `kubectl apply -f ingress-rate-limit.yaml -n infra`. Limits: 10req/s for non-prod-customer tags.

ops-bot: ingress config applied.

Mike: ingress throttling in place. seeing immediate reduction in incoming request rate by ~40%. Queue backlog growth slowed but still large.

Zoe: canary resource change passed basic health checks. Rolling out full resource patch to all dispatcher replicas.

Alex: rollout complete. Some older pods restarted. New pods accepted on nodes that had free memory. Queue depth dropped from 12.3k -> 7.1k over 6 minutes. Token latency from 800ms -> 420ms. Good.

Sara: cloud quota bumped to allow +10 nodes (pending until support confirms). If we get those nodes, we can autoscaler-resume normal behavior.

Mike: PD: Zoe acknowledged incident and manual mitigations in place. I'll update PD timeline and set a 30-min review window.

Zoe: customer impact summary for PD: partial degradation for high-throughput customers in region prod-2; increased latency and intermittent 503s for ~18 minutes; mitigation: manual scale + resource patch + ingress throttling. No data loss.

Alex: follow-up actions (post-incident): 1) audit node pool quotas and reserve burst capacity 2) make metrics-server rollout safer (canary to 1% then ramp) 3) autoscaler observability: alert on HPA ScalingFailed event 4) run chaos test for node-quota-exhaust scenarios.

Sara: adding these to incident doc and assigning owners. I'll create an incident report after PD closes.

Zoe: PD updated, moving to 'acknowledged -> mitigated' state. Leaving this thread open for any follow-ups. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Incident PD-INC-9801 status changed to: "Mitigated" - resolution notes updated by Zoe.

incident-bot: auto-summary: "manual scale + resource patch + ingress throttling mitigated queue backlog; root causes: metrics API partial outage + regional node quota exhaustion"

Zoe: final note: if you saw any related customer tickets, link them to PD-INC-9801. I'll start the postmortem doc.

Mike: thanks all.

Alex: good work.

Sara: filing follow-ups now.

ops-bot: Closing out automation checks. All systems nominal.
